title: Reduce dashboard read-amplification with time-bucketed indexes and hot-path caching
creator: Maya Chen
description: Investigate and implement a combined solution to reduce read-amplification for the Console dashboard query APIs. Current issue: heavy queries over long time ranges trigger full table scans or wide index scans that amplify IO and increase tail latency for other tenants. Goal is to lower median and p95 query latency for common dashboard queries (last 24h / 7d / 30d) while reducing backend CPU/IO cost by at least 40% for typical slices.
acceptance_criteria: Dashboard list and time-series endpoints for last-24h and last-7d: median latency < 150ms and p95 < 450ms under 1k qps synthetic workload
End-to-end egress cost per 10k dashboard requests reduced by >= 30% in staging compared to baseline
No regression in correctness: query results identical to baseline for sample prompts/tenants (tolerance: numerical rounding only)
Graceful fallback: if new index or cache is missing, system falls back to existing query path without error
Instrumentation added: cache hit ratio, index scan counts, read amplification factor, request coalescing stats
design_notes: High-level approach: combine time-bucketed materialized indexes with a small LRU hot-path cache and in-flight request coalescing to reduce duplicate work for concurrent identical queries.
Indexing: create composite index on (tenant_id, time_bucket_day, metric_type, event_time DESC) and a secondary index for 1-hour buckets for high-resolution recent queries.
Materialized aggregates: precompute daily/rolling-3h aggregates for heavy counters (tokens_generated, request_count) in the pipeline so dashboard queries can hit compact tables for longer ranges.

Caching: add a per-region in-memory LRU cache for query results with configurable TTLs: 30s for sub-hour queries, 5m for daily aggregates. Cache keys include tenant_id + route + time_range + query_filters + model_version.
Request coalescing: dedupe identical in-flight queries at the service layer using an in-memory promise map keyed by cache key to avoid stampeding herd on cache-miss.
Fallback semantics: if cache or precomputed aggregate is stale or missing, route to live query and asynchronously warm the cache; write operations should invalidate relevant keys via pub/sub.
Cost/consistency tradeoff: prefer eventual consistency for aggregates <=5m freshness; provide strict real-time path behind query param for customers that require it.
Security: index and cache keys respect tenant scoping; do not cache tenant-sensitive transient tokens or PII fields. Security review flagged for audit log of cache invalidations.
implementation_tasks: DB: Add migration to create time_bucket_day and time_bucket_hour columns and create composite indexes (SQL migration + rollback)
Pipeline: extend analytics ETL to emit daily and rolling-3h aggregates into materialized_aggregates table
API: implement cache layer in dashboard-query-service with LRU TTL config and consistent cache key builder
Service: add in-flight coalescing layer and unit tests for concurrent flows
Invalidate: wire cache invalidation via analytics-change pubsub topic for backfills/retrospective writes
Feature flag: gate the new query path behind feature flag console.timebucket_v1 for gradual rollout
Bench: add synthetic workload generator and k6 scenarios for last-24h, last-7d, and last-30d queries
Infra: increase staging DB read-replica size temporarily for migration verification
Docs: update Console API docs to document cache semantics and the new query parameter `fresh=true` for strict reads
qa_notes: Create tenant fixtures with realistic traffic shape (small/medium/large) and seed event_time across 90 days for validation

Verification steps: compare row-level results between baseline and new path for 50 queries per tenant slice; run fuzz tests with random filters; verify no stale data when writes occur within TTL window
Load test: run 60-minute soak at 1k rps hitting dashboard endpoints with mixed time ranges; collect p50/p95/p99 and compare to baseline
Chaos: introduce pubsub delivery delays to ensure cache invalidation still converges
Edge-cases: multi-tenant queries (org-admin view) should merge tenant-scoped materialized results without leakage
rollout_plan: Stage 1 (feature-flagged, canary): Enable new path for 5% of tenants in staging; monitor cache hit and read amplification metrics
Stage 2 (ramp): 25% production tenants after 48h of stable staging results; keep fallback enabled
Stage 3 (full): 100% production after 7 days and a successful perf SLA run; remove feature flag and clean up old indexes after 30 days
Rollback: flip feature flag off to restore old query path; have DB rollback migration available but run only if necessary
monitoring_and_metrics: New dashboards: cache_hit_ratio by route and tenant tier, time_bucket_index_scan_count, read_amplification (rows_read / rows_matched), api_latency_p50_p95_p99 by time_range
Alerts: p95 latency > 600ms for dashboard-query endpoint sustained for 5m; cache_hit_ratio < 20% for 30m for last-24h route
Cost metric: IO ops/sec and read bandwidth delta compared to baseline on read-replicas
Instrumentation: tag traces with path.variant (timebucket | live) and include index_used in DB spans
comments: 2026-03-02 Maya Chen: Initial spike showed 3.2x read amplification for month-range queries on large tenants. Decided to pursue time-bucketed indexes + materialized aggregates rather than complete denormalization.
2026-03-05 Diego Alvarez: Created SQL migration draft and local benchmark harness. Observed 2.1x improvement on small dataset when using day-buckets.
2026-03-08 Priya Natarajan (PM): Added acceptance criteria around cost reduction and rollback plan. Requested visibility to cost metrics in Console.
2026-03-10 Review (Infra): flagged that replicas need temporary scaling during migration; added infra task to implementation list.
2026-03-12 QA: early staging runs show cache hit ratio ~58% for last-24h queries and median latency drop from 320ms to 120ms. p95 improved but we still see tail spikes during backfills.
2026-03-14 Diego Alvarez: Implemented in-flight coalescing and pushed canary behind feature flag. Next: run 4-hour canary in staging and iterate on invalidation edges.
